clue.text: Politician's anger contained by American judges

indicators.note: contained by says the politician and the anger sit within the American letters

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A US politician's temper is being reined in by American judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires are the officials who rule on play in a game, acting as its judges.

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, rubbish means worthless or of no help

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase splits into an order to cut consumption, and as one word it is a synonym of worthless.

parts.note: to pat is to hit lightly
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: An old pop song was a hit by Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pop hit by the band Queen; 'pop' is really a father, and pater is the old, schoolboy Latin for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is an old-fashioned, public-school word for one's father or dad.

clue.text: Playboy's grand inside — it makes one's cheeks red!

indicators.note: inside says the grand goes within the playboy's letters

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man about town, a playboy
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A playboy has a thousand stuffed in his pocket, and it makes his cheeks blush.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is red make-up applied to colour the cheeks.

parts.note: smart means clever or shrewd
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone was stung by a sharp-witted reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: If something smarted it hurt with a sharp pain, as a sting does.

clue.text: Unholy acts in a bizarre order

indicators.note: put in a bizarre order means the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Unholy rituals are carried out in a strange sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre order' rearranges the seven letters of 'acts in a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, belonging to Satan, so wicked and unholy.

indicators.note: catching says the manoeuvre word holds the navy letters

parts.note: to steer is to manoeuvre a vessel
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval manoeuvre turns out harder than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterner means stricter, exacting more from people.

clue.text: Pretty good ball or tee shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: A golf ball struck off the tee was a fairly decent stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like the golf stroke but signals an anagram of BALLORTEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means acceptable, fairly good without being excellent.

clue.text: Pining again, lost in a daze

indicators.note: a mind in a daze is muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone yearns once more, wandering confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a daze' rearranges AGAIN and LOST together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for the past, a kind of pining.

clue.text: Most fashionable bird embracing the French

indicators.note: embracing means the bird's letters wrap around the French article

parts.note: a coot is a water bird
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: The trendiest bird is hugging a French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolest is slang for trendiest, most stylish.

indicators.note: strangely means the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A train is strangely punctual for once.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Train's is a link. 'Train' is the people following a celebrity, not a railway, and 'on' here is fodder for the anagram, not a position word.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a retinue, the train of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Means to catch girl with nothing on

indicators.note: on places the nothing after the girl in this across clue

parts.note: lass is a girl
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A naked girl is the way to catch someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Disguising a sneer, Tory leader's serious

indicators.note: disguising means the letters are changed into another shape
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Conservative leader hides a sneer and looks grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disguising' rearranges A SNEER into EARNES, then 'leader's' takes T from Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intent.

indicators.note: up in an across clue means the word is read backwards

parts.note: torn in the sense of tore along, rushed, as ran
to scoff is to eat greedily, so ate

explanation.surface: A Republican tore up the recount and wolfed it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAN to NAR; 'Recount' is the verb tell, not a second count of votes.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate a story is to tell or relate it in sequence.

clue.text: Resignation blunder brought up in split

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to sunder is to split apart

indicators.note: brought up means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A resignation mistake is raised at a party split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resignation' means giving in, not quitting a job; 'brought up' reverses the blunder word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender is giving in, accepting defeat, a resignation to one's fate.

parts.note: a rotter is a scoundrel

indicators.note: flipping says the word is flipped over, read in reverse

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A rogue goes completely mad over a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like mild swearing but turns MAD to DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is the great Dutch seaport.

parts.note: to elect is to choose
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Select the correct wiring for a terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor at which current enters or leaves, a terminal.

clue.text: He's unreasonably opposed to British colony's return

indicators.note: return means the words come back in reverse order

parts.note: Gib is short for Gibraltar, a British territory once called a colony

explanation.surface: A man unreasonably objects to a British colony coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is a person intolerantly, unreasonably prejudiced against others.

parts.note: to trim is to cut
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An attractive girl is slim, in other words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is slang for an attractive, sweet person.

indicators.note: in places King George within the succession

parts.note: a chain is a series, a succession
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: King George is shamed within the royal succession.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or embarrassment at failure, close to shame.

clue.text: Let off former husband with single payment

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
single means one
a rate is a charge or payment

explanation.surface: Clear an ex-husband who settles with one lump sum.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear of blame, letting someone off.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, eavesdrops or listens in secretly

explanation.walkthrough: The second 'bugs' is a verb: to earwig is an old word for to eavesdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pincered insects are loosely called bugs, and eavesdropping on someone is an old verb sense too.

clue.text: Driving out for Sunday trip outside

indicators.note: outside means the trip is placed around the Sunday letter

parts.note: an outing is a trip

explanation.surface: Drive out for a Sunday excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting means expelling or forcing someone out.

parts.note: ever means always
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Sweets always make you gain weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club nicknamed the Toffees, not sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Toffees is the long-standing nickname of the Merseyside football club.

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
better means preferable, more desirable

explanation.surface: The magazine piece praises a superior fashion accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accessory' is the legal sense, an accomplice, not a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: An accessory to a crime is someone who helps the culprit, an abetter.

definitions.meaning: to ooze or discharge a fluid, as a gland does

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one is from secret, the other from secretion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding something away and a gland producing fluid are both senses of the same spelling.

indicators.note: inside places the right letter within the other pieces

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler wonders if the catch is safely stowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the angler's basket with the catch inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket an angler keeps the catch in.

parts.note: eras are periods, dates in history
the heart, middle letter, of sweet is E

explanation.surface: Cancel the dates with a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to delete, wiping something out or cancelling it.

parts.note: a set playing music, tuned to the BBC stations numbered one, two or three

explanation.walkthrough: BBC Radio 1, 2 and 3 are British national stations: pop, easy listening and classical.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set brings music and is tuned to numbered national stations.

clue.text: Wandering from one's point on sermon

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tine is a prong or point of a fork or antler
a rant is a ranting harangue, a sermon

explanation.surface: Someone drifting off the point in a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant means travelling from place to place, roving.

definitions.meaning: a book of the Old Testament, in the Good Book

explanation.walkthrough: The Good Book is the Bible; its fourth book has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are characters, and the fourth book of the Bible bears this title.

parts.note: brass means cheek, impudence, which is gall
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A ship's brass fittings take ages to polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is nerve or cheek here, not metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the 16th and 17th centuries.
